title: Flamingo Lantern Thermal Lift Simulator
description: A flamingo stands on a platform surrounded by floating lanterns that generate rising thermal columns. The user must ignite lanterns in the correct sequence and adjust their heat intensity to create a combined thermal updraft strong enough to lift the flamingo into flight, while keeping air temperature within safe biological limits.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls from CDN. Load Lantern.glb and flamingo.glb from shared_assets/. Scene setup: place the flamingo model at ground level on a circular stone platform. Arrange 5 lantern instances in a pentagon formation around the flamingo at ground level, each labeled L1-L5 with HTML overlay labels. Add a dark twilight sky background (gradient or color), ambient light (low intensity 0.15), and a directional moonlight. Camera starts at position (0, 8, 18) looking at origin. Physics simulation: each lantern has an 'ignited' boolean and a 'heatIntensity' float (0.0-1.0). When ignited, a lantern emits an orange point light and spawns upward-drifting particle sprites simulating heat shimmer. Implement a simplified thermal model: total lift force equals the sum of all ignited lanterns' heatIntensity values. The flamingo lifts off when total lift exceeds 3.2 but the combined temperature must stay below 4.5 to avoid overheating (show a red warning). Interactions (6-8 steps): clicking a lantern toggles its ignited state. A slider panel appears for each ignited lantern to adjust heatIntensity from 0.1 to 1.0 in 0.1 increments. Display a real-time HUD showing: total lift force, temperature sum, flamingo altitude, and status (grounded/ascending/overheated). When lift threshold is met and temperature is safe, animate the flamingo rising with a gentle wing-flap animation (use the morph targets from the GLB if available, otherwise oscillate rotation.z). Add a 'Reset' button to extinguish all lanterns and return the flamingo to ground. Validate that users cannot set intensity above 1.0 or below 0.1. Show a success banner when flamingo reaches altitude 15 units. The flamingo should descend smoothly if lanterns are extinguished mid-flight using simple gravity deceleration.
